video_title: Denver Nuggets Full Practice Media Availability | 10.13.26

quotes.speaker: Daron Holmes II
quotes.summary_phrase: Daron Holmes II on his role as a five
quotes.excerpt: on offense you're the vocal point, so you have to be able to get into action
quotes.quote: For the five, on offense you're the vocal point, so you have to be able to get into action a lot, come up and set a lot of screens. On defense you have to be the anchor. It's very important. It's very challenging, but it's fun and that's why we're here.
quotes.social_post: Daron Holmes II on his transition to playing the five for the Nuggets: On offense you are the focal point and have to get into action, but on defense you have to be the anchor. It is very challenging but it is fun.

quotes.speaker: Daron Holmes II
quotes.summary_phrase: Daron Holmes II on the importance of screening for guards
quotes.excerpt: our job is to get them open, so setting a great hard screen for them
quotes.quote: We got guards like Jamal, we have guys that can score the ball and they're very good at what they do. Our job is to get them open, so setting a great hard screen for them and getting out quick puts a lot of pressure on that five man and the defense to be able to guard them as well.
quotes.social_post: Daron Holmes II emphasizes the importance of setting hard screens for Jamal Murray and the Nuggets guards to put pressure on the opposing defense.

quotes.speaker: Daron Holmes II
quotes.summary_phrase: Daron Holmes II on playing with Tyus Jones
quotes.excerpt: as a big you should love playing with them and Ryan, even Jamal
quotes.quote: Tyus is very well, especially pass-first. As a big you should love playing with them and Ryan, even Jamal. Jamal can score the ball all three levels, but those guys they create for others and Tyus does such a great job of getting everybody open, getting everybody involved. He's a leader, he's a talker. You need guys like that on your team and that's why he's been the NBA for such a long time because he does it at such a high level.
quotes.social_post: Daron Holmes II praises new teammate Tyus Jones: He is a pass-first leader who does a great job of getting everybody open and involved.

quotes.speaker: Daron Holmes II
quotes.summary_phrase: Daron Holmes II on the conditioning of Aaron Gordon and Christian Braun
quotes.excerpt: he took the whole summer to really work on his body
quotes.quote: I'll start with AG. He took the whole summer to really work on his body. He rehabbed mentally, physically, because that was his biggest thing last year is being injured. I think he's done a very good job of this now. He's not missing as many practices, he's been locked in, he's been involved. With Cam Johnson, me and him we go back before this, so I stay at his place sometimes when we go back to Arizona over the summer. I've been able to see his workouts, so he's always locked in, he's always doing the right things, he eats the right way, he's going to Pilates. He's doing the stuff he needs to do to get ready.
quotes.social_post: Daron Holmes II says Aaron Gordon has been locked in and healthy this offseason while noting that Cam Johnson is doing everything right to prepare for the season.

quotes.speaker: Tyus Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyus Jones on the importance of plus-minus for bench units
quotes.excerpt: plus-minus is a huge indicator of a bench unit and so we want to make sure
quotes.quote: Plus-minus is a huge indicator of a bench unit and so we want to make sure we're in that plus side, allowing them to get their rest, allowing them to make sure they're fresh come fourth quarters and come late in the season too. It's a long season, so we just want to make sure we're doing our part as a bench unit.
quotes.social_post: Tyus Jones on the bench unit goal: Plus-minus is a huge indicator for us. We want to make sure we are in the plus side to keep the starters fresh for the fourth quarter.

quotes.speaker: Tyus Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyus Jones on playing against Trey Lyles
quotes.excerpt: it's a blessing every single time. It's something that I don't take for granted
quotes.quote: It's a blessing every single time. It's something that I don't take for granted, our family doesn't take for granted. Family is always at every single game. We'll be going to Chicago in November and my wife and kids are going out there and getting the cousins all together and mom, aunt and uncle, brother, everyone comes out for the game. So it's something that we don't take lightly, we don't take for granted.
quotes.social_post: Tyus Jones discusses the importance of family support and the blessing of playing professional basketball.

quotes.speaker: Tyus Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyus Jones on team offensive styles
quotes.excerpt: there's a handful of teams that are more just dribble-drive based where they're just spreading the floor out
quotes.quote: There's a handful of teams that are more just dribble-drive based where they're just spreading the floor out, guy with the ball is trying to put his head down, touch the paint and create that domino that way. I think there's a number of teams who are getting into a pick and roll or a guard-to-guard screen type action, try to create a domino effect that way.
quotes.social_post: Tyus Jones breaks down modern NBA offensive styles, noting the shift between dribble-drive systems and guard-to-guard screen actions to create a domino effect.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on simplifying the playbook for the bench
quotes.excerpt: I don't want to overload a playbook because you want to simplify things for guys
quotes.quote: I don't want to overload a playbook because you want to simplify things for guys. That's the challenge is the other guys, it's too much, too fast. The IQ is really high, the way they've been defended even these preseason games, the conversations you have with them, it's a different level. Script today was a different level because they've been doing it for so long. So with the second group you got to really calm down.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman on managing the Nuggets second unit: The challenge is not to overload the playbook. You have to really calm down and simplify things for the second group.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on Julian Strawther's growth
quotes.excerpt: I think he's attempting to do things defensively different. I thought he struggled a little bit
quotes.quote: I think he's attempting to do things defensively different. I thought he struggled a little bit in the first half the other night against Chicago, was much better in the second half. He's got to be able to guard his matchup. We know what he can do offensively, he's a great ATO player, great second side player as far as like the dribble handoffs, all those things. So I see a lot of what I've always seen. I think the growth has to come with the consistency defensively.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman on Julian Strawther: We know what he can do offensively, but the growth has to come with the consistency defensively.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on playing Tyus Jones and Jamal Murray together
quotes.excerpt: we had to do it in the playoffs a little bit. You're obviously giving up something
quotes.quote: We had to do it in the playoffs a little bit. You're obviously giving up something when you do that, which is size. Some of these teams you play that play the bigger guards, it's tough defensively, but offensively it makes a lot of sense getting Jamal off the ball. It's not just such a grind for him. Especially when Aaron is off the floor like last year he was playing. Always helps to have a ball handler to relieve Jamal a little bit.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman on playing Tyus Jones and Jamal Murray together: It makes a lot of sense offensively to get Jamal off the ball and relieve him, even if it costs us some size defensively.
